plan.chapter_thesis: Active modulation mechanisms spanning phase-change materials, liquid crystals, MEMS actuators, graphene, and electro-optic polymers enable real-time holographic reconfiguration but each imposes distinct penalties on diffraction efficiency, spectral bandwidth, or modulation depth, creating a fundamental speed-efficiency-bandwidth trilemma that constrains practical dynamic metasurface holographic displays.
plan.reader_takeaway: No single active material platform currently solves the speed-efficiency-bandwidth trilemma; selecting a modulation mechanism requires accepting specific trade-offs between switching speed, optical efficiency, and spectral range based on the target application.

argument_sequence.purpose: Establish the limitation of static metasurfaces to motivate the necessity of active modulation for dynamic holography.
Introduce phase-change materials (PCMs) as a mechanism for non-volatile reconfiguration and define their impact on efficiency and speed.
Examine liquid crystal and electro-optic polymer platforms for continuous phase tuning and their bandwidth limitations.
Analyze MEMS and elastic reconfiguration for large mechanical displacement versus speed constraints.
Evaluate graphene and carrier-injection mechanisms for high-speed modulation with associated efficiency losses.
Synthesize the performance metrics across platforms to explicitly define the speed-efficiency-bandwidth trilemma.

terminology_rows.note: Materials like GST or VO2 that switch between amorphous and crystalline states to alter refractive index non-volatily.
The fundamental constraint where optimizing one parameter (e.g., speed) inherently degrades at least one other (efficiency or bandwidth) in active metasurfaces.
Systems using mechanical deformation (MEMS or stretchable substrates) to physically alter meta-atom geometry for phase control.

explanation_block_rows.title: The Static Baseline and Need for Dynamics
explanation_block_rows.goal: Define the operational ceiling of static metasurfaces to establish why active modulation is required for holographic displays.

explanation_block_rows.title: Non-Volatile Switching via Phase-Change Materials
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain the mechanism of PCM-based modulation, highlighting its high contrast but limited switching speed and cyclability.

explanation_block_rows.title: Continuous Tuning with Liquid Crystals and Polymers
explanation_block_rows.goal: Describe how LCs and electro-optic polymers provide analog phase control, noting their spectral bandwidth restrictions and response times.

explanation_block_rows.title: Mechanical Reconfiguration and MEMS Actuators
explanation_block_rows.goal: Detail the use of mechanical actuation for large phase shifts, contrasting high efficiency with slow mechanical response limits.

explanation_block_rows.title: High-Speed Carrier Modulation in Graphene and Semiconductors
explanation_block_rows.goal: Assess electronic modulation methods for ultrafast switching, addressing the trade-off with absorption losses and reduced diffraction efficiency.

explanation_block_rows.title: Synthesizing the Performance Trilemma
explanation_block_rows.goal: Integrate findings to demonstrate that no single platform dominates all three axes (speed, efficiency, bandwidth), defining the current technological bottleneck.

responsibility_coverage_rows.responsibility: Cover active modulation mechanisms (PCM, LC, MEMS, Graphene, Polymers)
responsibility_coverage_rows.note: Blocks 2-5 individually address each required material platform.
Block 6 synthesizes the trade-offs; Block 1 establishes the baseline need.
